Current queue review,20October2026 (bd-01M5E33RPWBT8NAGKCKJMMN6FN)

Completeness: probe_audit_not_complete.
Assessment: Historical findings concern incremental recompilation and Mirror coverage; clean CI evidence does not establish incremental invalidation coverage. No fresh bypass demonstrated.
Staleness: Title count12of21 is a historical sample, not a current inventory. Consolidated children must not be treated as completed audit work.
Remaining / next action: Inventory actual compile-time probes and non-string anchors, then add missing Mirror/anchor controls with one incremental mutation per affected module. Recount before making any current coverage claim.
Audit: docs/refactor/evidence/queue-review-20261020/README.md. This planning review does not grant publication, study-read or integration authority.

--- Preserved prior scope, acceptance and history ---

Current release queue, 7 October 2026: release-later; milestone-maintenance.
Plan: docs/refactor/RELEASE-QUEUE.md. Mote remains authoritative; one primary agent and at most one helper.

Reconciliation: Atlas Mirror probes are present. Three children closed by consolidation moved work back here; other closed children do not establish this audit. Inspected guarded types remain private non-case classes; no current construction bypass demonstrated.

Remaining / next action: Finish the tools audit for missing non-string construction-probe dependencies and companion-versus-Mirror coverage; repair the remaining RecallGraph/population summon probes and features/interview/align anchoring, with one incremental mutation witness per affected module.

Release tags schedule work; they do not establish completion or empirical qualification. Use current AGENTS.md for ownership, scoped gates and exact-SHA review; old fleet roles, timers and fixed gate task counts are historical. Keep the original scientific preregistration, denominators, admission and sealed-test rules below.

Retained acceptance and design context:

Scheduling lane: maintenance. Current plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md. Live dependency edges supersede historical sequencing below.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19; governing docs/refactor/PLAN.md.
Keep open: nine dependency anchors landed but three did not; Mirror.ProductOf coverage is a separate property from dependency anchoring. Audit actual remaining named doors; no blanket sweep completion claim.

Original scope retained below for evidence; fleet procedure/assignments are historical and do not govern single-developer work.

SCALA 3 HAS TWO fromProduct DOORS AND OUR PROBES COVER THEM UNEVENLY. Raised by
codex-storymodel-collab while sharpening the construction-boundary rule; measured by me across all
21 typeCheckErrors suites.

  the companion's own `T.fromProduct(...)`
  `summon[scala.deriving.Mirror.ProductOf[T]].fromProduct(...)`

MEASURED: 12 of 21 probe suites test the companion door and NOT the summon door. Among them
AtlasConstructionBoundarySuite, which guards SurfaceAtlas and TranscriptAtlas -- two of the ten
types sweep 2 closed tonight -- plus RecallGraphUnforgeableSuite and PopulationBoundarySuite.
`.apply(` appears in ZERO suites, though for a private-constructor type Scala 3 makes the generated
apply private too, so that door may not exist; worth confirming rather than assuming.

SEVERITY, STATED HONESTLY BEFORE ANYONE PANICS: this is a TEST-COVERAGE gap, not a live hole. All
ten sweep-2 types are `final class ... private`, and Scala 3 derives no Mirror.ProductOf for a
non-case class, so the summon door does not exist for them. The probes matter as REGRESSION guards:
if someone converts one back to a case class, a companion-door probe catches it, and the summon
probe is a second independent witness. I am not claiming the sealing is incomplete.

THE MODEL TO COPY IS align/consumer/AlignBoundarySuite.scala:14-34. It probes BOTH doors and carries
a real positive control -- `AlignForgeControl`, a case class whose Mirror.fromProduct is asserted to
COMPILE with `assertEquals(errors, Nil)` and is then actually forged, so the probe demonstrably can
fail. That is the standard; a refusal beside a control that does not compile proves nothing.

SCOPE OF THIS BEAD: add the summon-door probe to AtlasConstructionBoundarySuite for SurfaceAtlas and
TranscriptAtlas, reusing the positive control the suite already has. The remaining eleven suites are
follow-up and should be listed, not swept in one candidate.
